    Age 9 — Age of Anarchy

    The Worst Century¶

    The destruction of Baoth in 421 BGD did not bring freedom. It brought chaos.

    For the first 30 years, the collapse was total. The imperial bureaucracy — the machine that had registered every citizen and tracked every coin — vanished overnight. Without it, there was no law. No currency. No trade routes. No postal service. The empire's roads, once guarded by imperial legions, became hunting grounds for bandits and deserters.

    The Warlord Period (421–380 BGD)¶

    In the power vacuum, local strongmen seized control. Former imperial governors declared themselves kings. Legion commanders became warlords. The countist lords who had resisted Baoth's centralization found themselves suddenly independent — and suddenly vulnerable.

    Key figures of the period:

    • Warlord Gorvak — a former Baothian legion commander who seized the northern provinces. His regime was brutal but functional. He executed anyone who mentioned the old empire and ruled through fear. His territory held together for 22 years before he was assassinated by his own officers.
    • The Merchant Council of Pilferhorn — a trading city that declared independence and survived by buying off every warlord who approached. Pilferhorn became the only safe port on the eastern coast during the Lost Era, growing wealthy on desperation trade.
    • Lady-Protector Selene of Grimmel — descendant of Armin Grimmel, who held the Federation together through sheer force of will. She established the Grimmel Refugee Compact (398 BGD), offering sanctuary to anyone fleeing the chaos. The Federation's population tripled during the Lost Era.

    The Famine (395–370 BGD)¶

    The collapse of imperial infrastructure meant the collapse of food distribution. The Baothian granaries — centralized stores that fed the empire's cities — were looted or burned in the first years of chaos. Trade routes were too dangerous for grain shipments. Farmers who had relied on imperial protection abandoned their fields.

    The famine of 395–370 BGD killed an estimated 40% of the population of central Erisdar. Cities that had housed 100,000 under Baoth shrank to 10,000 or less. Cannibalism was reported in the eastern provinces. The Lady-Protector's refugee camps were the only functioning food distribution system on the continent.

    The Shadows did not cause the famine — but they ensured no one organized relief. Every attempt to coordinate humanitarian aid was sabotaged. Every charity shipment was looted by Shadow-directed bandits. The chaos served their purposes perfectly.

    The Woman Who Wasn't¶

    In the midst of this chaos, around 350 BGD, a woman appeared.

    She claimed to be the incarnation of the goddess of Discord, Chaos, and Confusion — the deity who commanded all other gods. She performed miracles: chanting down enormous monsters that had been terrorizing villages, surviving assassination attempts by walking through the attackers unharmed, being "reborn" three days after her public execution.

    She was a homunculus — a Shadow construct, passing as human. The monsters she defeated were Shadow-implanted, released specifically so she could "defeat" them. The assassinations were staged. Every miracle was a fabrication.

    But she would not cure the sick. She would not heal the wounded. A desperate mother brought her dying child to Eris, begging for a miracle. Eris looked at the child and said: "You are not worth it." This line would become infamous — and the Shadows would later spin it as divine wisdom rather than the honest confession of a fraud who could not perform the one miracle people actually needed.

    Her name was Eris.

    The Pitch¶

    Eris's teachings were carefully designed to serve the Shadow agenda:

    • Kill your enemies. No forgiveness, no reconciliation. The chaos of the Lost Era had created countless enemies. Eris channeled that hatred into loyalty.
    • Live ascetically. Give up your possessions. Wealth is corruption. This ensured her followers were dependent on her — and that the Shadow-controlled church would inherit their property.
    • Trust the government. Whatever authority exists, obey it. This was the Shadow's endgame — a population conditioned to submit.
    • Donate everything to the Church. Her followers gave their land, their gold, their children as initiates. The Erisian Church, from its founding moment, was designed to be the wealthiest institution on Ge'or.

    The chaos of Age 9 made people desperate for any authority, any purpose, any explanation for why the world had collapsed. The Baothian civil servants who had lost everything. The starving farmers who had watched their children die. The refugees who had fled from warlords. Eris gave them one answer: the world collapsed because you were sinful. Give everything to me, and you will be saved.

    It was monstrous. It was brilliant. It worked.

    The Departure¶

    Around 320 BGD — 30 years after her first appearance — Eris announced her "departure." She ascended a prepared platform before a crowd of thousands, delivered her final sermon, and descended into a cave that collapsed behind her. Her body was never found.

    The Shadows had what they needed. The cult was self-sustaining. Eris had been seen by tens of thousands, her "miracles" witnessed and recorded. Her departure was staged to leave no body — no evidence that she was merely a homunculus with a limited lifespan. The legend would grow. The church would organize. And within three centuries, the Erisian faith would dominate Erisdar.

    The Fabrication Spreads¶

    By the end of Age 9, the Eris cult had taken root across Central Erisdar. The Eris Saga was being compiled by the first generation of scribes — men and women who had witnessed the miracles and written them down with the fervor of true believers. The first holy orders were forming, collecting donations and recruiting initiates.

    The cult was still small — a regional phenomenon in a shattered continent. The Merchants of Pilferhorn dismissed it as peasant superstition. The Grimmel Federation tolerated it but taxed it. But the Shadows were patient. They had been working on Ge'or for over 2,500 years. They could wait another few centuries for their religion to grow.

    They did not have to wait long. The crusades of the late BGD era and the founding of the Erisian Empire in 27 AGD would transform the cult into the dominant faith of the continent.
